commits.message:
[AMD][GFX1250-strict] Enable HW-accelerated block32 scaled_upcast (#12499)

GFX1250-strict only supports Block32 opcodes for hardware instructions for scaled upcast. Layouts which require block16 will go through the software path.

commits.comment: FPSan 的 i8 MMA 分解只在 CUDA 目标上启用。原实现仅用 getAMDArch 排除 AMD，导致 out-of-tree 后端（如 NPU）也会被重写成它无法 lowering 的 #ttg.nvidia_mma layout。改为读取 module 的 ttg.target 属性，前缀不是 'cuda' 就返回 false。CUDA 与 AMD 行为不变，属于通用 sanitizer pass 的目标判定修正，改动很小但语义清晰。

ascend_impact.functionality: 无影响（该改动实际是让 FPSan 的 i8 MMA 分解不再作用于非 CUDA 目标，对 Ascend 后端是豁免而非破坏；triton-ascend 不启用 FPSan 该路径）

commits.message:
[FPSan] Only use the i8 MMA decomposition on CUDA targets (#12198)

The i8 MMA decomposition emits `#ttg.nvidia_mma` layouts but was only
skipped for AMD, so out-of-tree backends get NVIDIA layouts they can't

Keep it to CUDA targets - CUDA and AMD behave as before.

commits.message:
[AMD] Move MIR dump/swap to AMD CodeGen stage (#12528)

Last of the three changes started in #12123 and #12122. Calls the entry
points #12122 added and deletes what they replace: translateLLVMIRToMIR,
translateMIRToASM and their m.def bindings in python/src/llvm.cc, plus
third_party/amd/lib/Target/MIRDAG/, which existed only to serve that
path.

compiler.py gains translate_to_mir and translate_mir_to_asm next to
compile_amdgpu, sharing the serialization and options helpers. The
wrapper assembles the dump file from the two returned buffers, so the
on-disk format is byte-for-byte unchanged and existing tooling keeps
working.

Testing: test_mir_stage.py and test_knobs.py pass on gfx950 against the
downloaded artifact. Dump then swap the unmodified MIR back gives AMDGCN
byte-identical to compile_amdgpu; the same swap with the machine
scheduler disabled differs, confirming the swap really drives the
scheduler's slot.

On gfx1250 the whole dump -> reschedule -> swap -> run loop was
exercised on a ~17k-instruction GEMM: a byte-identical re-emission still
runs, a large legal reordering still computes the right answer, and an
order respecting no dependence at all is rejected.

test_dag_matches_llvm now skips unless AMD_LLVM_BUILD_DIR points at an
llc from the code generator's LLVM. It used to fall back to Triton's
core llc or a system one; both are different revisions and reject the
MIR, and the prebuilt package ships no llc. The cross-check therefore
only runs in a source build.

MIR files dumped before this change came out of a different LLVM and are
not expected to parse under TRITON_SWAP_MIR. Regenerate them.

[AMD][Gluon] Move gfx9 CachePolicy to cdna3/cdna4 namespaces (#12526)

Expose the gfx9 CachePolicy directly as amd.cdna3.CachePolicy and
amd.cdna4.CachePolicy instead of under the buffer submodules, since it

commits.comment: 用 RAII guard 取代 armLivePipelineDAGEmission/disarmLivePipelineDAGEmission 这对函数：LivePipelineDAGEmission 构造时保存外层 sink、析构时恢复（而非置 nullptr），从而支持单线程嵌套，并把'guard 生命周期必须覆盖 addPassesToEmitFile 与 PassManager::run'这一约束搬到调用点的类型系统上。同步更新 DAGBuilder.h 的 include guard 与注释、两个调用点（llvm.cc 与 amdgpu_codegen.cc 去掉 scope_exit）、以及 amd-llvm-build-info.json 的 build_number。功能等价，属于 AMD codegen 内部代码质量改进。
commits.message:
[AMD] Scope live MIR DAG emission with an RAII guard (#12519)

Follows #12122. No functional change for the existing callers, which
already armed and disarmed around a single addPassesToEmitFile plus
PassManager run.

armLivePipelineDAGEmission/disarmLivePipelineDAGEmission are replaced by
a LivePipelineDAGEmission guard that saves the enclosing sink on
construction and restores it on destruction.

The sink is read at two different moments: pipeline construction, when
the TargetPassConfig callback substitutes the emitting pass for the
machine scheduler, and pipeline execution, when that pass writes the
DAG. The arm window has to span both, on one thread. A guard whose
lifetime is that window states the requirement at the call site instead
of in a header comment, and makes the pairing impossible to forget.

disarm also reset the sink to null rather than to its previous value, so
a nested arm on one thread silently disabled the enclosing one. Saving
and restoring removes that limitation instead of documenting it.

Bumps the code generator's build_number so the artifact picks up the
change.

commits.comment: AMD codegen 的 LLVM 依赖 bump 到 08b05a3352ee，_AMDGPUCodegenOptions 结构新增 enable_misched / emit_object 两个字段并把 codegenABIVersion 从 1 提到 2（必须与 amdgpu_codegen.cc 中的版本号一致）。这是为后续把 MIR dump/swap 迁入独立 codegen 库做的 ABI 准备，结构体布局变更属于强耦合点。

commits.comment: 移除编译器对 can_reorder 的支持，前端保留该参数以兼容。TT_ReshapeOp 删除 allow_reorder 属性、builder 的 allowReorder 参数与 assemblyFormat 相应段；DialectInferLayoutInterface::inferReshapeOpEncoding 去掉 allowReorder 形参（Gluon 与 TritonGPU 两个实现同步）；ReshapeOp::build/verify/canonicalize/fold 不再依赖该属性；TritonGPU 的 CanonicalizeConvertFromReshape 与 CanonicalizeConvertFromConvert 中基于 allowReorder 的重写被删除，OptimizeThreadLocality 的 OptimizeReshapeLayoutPattern 与 Utility.cpp 的 canUseResultEncoding 分支整体删除；TritonSemantic.reshape 与 GluonSemantic.reshape 去掉 can_reorder（Gluon 不再做 not-supported 检查）；language/core.py 的 reshape/view/dot 与 standard.py 的 ravel 保留参数但忽略；python/src/ir.cc 的 create_reshape 去掉 allowReorder；InterpreterBuilder.create_reshape 同步；大量 lit/pytest 用例改为不再带 allow_reorder 并产生 layout 变化（出现了 convert_layout 与 linear layout）。影响面广，属跨后端 IR 语义清理。

ascend_impact.functionality: 命中必然影响路径。python/triton/language/semantic.py 的 TritonSemantic.reshape 签名由 reshape(input, dst_shape, can_reorder) 改为 reshape(input, dst_shape)，而 triton-ascend 的 _apply_ascend_patch 用 _patched_dot 覆写 TritonSemantic.dot，其内部若构造/转发 reshape 调用（含 multi-rank dot 的 batch 展平路径）会因参数数量不匹配抛 TypeError；同时 dot 的 reduce 路径中 reduction(axis=None) 也对 reshape 调用签名敏感。python/src/ir.cc 的 TritonOpBuilder.create_reshape 不再接受 allowReorder，AscendNPUIROpBuilder 若通过该绑定创建 reshape 需同步。include/triton/Dialect/Triton/IR/TritonOps.td 中 TT_ReshapeOp 删除 allow_reorder 属性并改变 assemblyFormat，直接改动 TTIR 定义——Ascend 复用 AST→TTIR 前端且 TritonToLinalg 以 TTIR 为输入；同时 ReshapeOp 的 canonicalize（reshape(expand_dims)/reshape(reshape)）与 fold 行为变化（不再有 allow_reorder 分支，且两段 reshape 合并时不再传播 reorder 语义）会改变 Ascend 收到的 IR 形态。lib/Dialect/Gluon 与 TritonGPU 的实现改动不影响 Ascend。
ascend_impact.testing: triton-ascend 需检查所有会走 reshape 的路径：dot 的多维 batch 展平（core.py 内 _semantic.reshape 调用点被改）、reduction(axis=None) 的展平、以及 TritonToLinalg 对 tt.reshape 的解析（assemblyFormat 变更后旧文本 IR 无法解析）。现有 lit 用例若含 tt.reshape ... allow_reorder 将解析失败。
suggested_test_areas: third_party/ascend/lib (TritonToLinalg reshape 相关 pass 与 lit 用例)
third_party/ascend/unittest/pytest_ut (含 dot/reduce 的算子用例)

commits.message:
Remove can_reorder (#12521)

Remove can_reorder from the compiler while keeping the flag in the
frontend for backward compatibility.

affected_interfaces: triton::DialectInferLayoutInterface::inferReshapeOpEncoding (include/triton/Dialect/Triton/IR/Dialect.h) — pure-virtual signature drops the `bool allowReorder` parameter; triton-ascend implements it in GluonInferLayoutInterface (lib/Dialect/Gluon/IR/Dialect.cpp:76) and TritonGPUInferLayoutInterface (lib/Dialect/TritonGPU/IR/Dialect.cpp:3047)
triton::ReshapeOp (include/triton/Dialect/Triton/IR/TritonOps.td) — `allow_reorder` UnitAttr removed; builders/`ReshapeOp::create` drop the `allowReorder` arg; `getAllowReorder()` accessor removed
deep_analysis.adaptation_guide:
This is a breaking C++ interface change plus a Python frontend/IR-API change, and triton-ascend depends on the removed APIs in both its vendored triton core and its Ascend-specific passes. Required changes:

1) C++ interface overrides (signature must drop the bool):
   - lib/Dialect/Gluon/IR/Dialect.cpp:76 `GluonInferLayoutInterface::inferReshapeOpEncoding`
   - lib/Dialect/TritonGPU/IR/Dialect.cpp:3047 `TritonGPUInferLayoutInterface::inferReshapeOpEncoding`

2) ReshapeOp tablegen + core op (mirror upstream d364bf19639a):
   - include/triton/Dialect/Triton/IR/TritonOps.td:472-485 remove `allow_reorder` UnitAttr, builder's `allowReorder` CArg, and the `allow_reorder` assemblyFormat alternative
   - lib/Dialect/Triton/IR/Ops.cpp:810-893 update `ReshapeOp::build`, `canonicalize` (reshape(reshape) folding), `fold`, and `verify` to drop `getAllowReorder()`/`allowReorder`
   - lib/Dialect/TritonGPU/IR/Ops.cpp:108-130 and 295-320 remove the `CanonicalizeConvertFromReshape` allow-reorder folding and the `cvt(reshape)->reshape` pattern that rely on `getAllowReorder()` (delete `hasEncoding`/`hasDotOperandEncoding` helpers that become unused)

3) Transforms/passes (Ascend-specific logic that must be reworked, not just signature-fixed):
   - lib/Dialect/TritonGPU/Transforms/OptimizeThreadLocality.cpp: delete `OptimizeReshapeLayoutPattern` (line ~30-80, removed upstream) and update `ReshapeOp::create(..., /*allowReorder=*/true, ...)` call at ~460
   - lib/Dialect/TritonGPU/Transforms/RemoveLayoutConversions.cpp:202 rework the layout-anchor heuristic `return reshape.getAllowReorder()`
   - lib/Dialect/TritonGPU/Transforms/Utility.cpp:470-510 & 640-650 drop `op.getAllowReorder()` from `inferReshapeOpDstEncoding`/`inferDstEncoding`/`inferSrcEncoding` and remove the reshape branch in `canUseResultEncoding`
   - lib/Dialect/Triton/Transforms/Combine.cpp:190 remove the `reshapeOp.getAllowReorder()` guard
   - lib/Dialect/TritonGPU/Transforms/DecomposeScaledBlocked.cpp and OptimizeDotOperands.cpp: drop the `allowReorder` argument from `ReshapeOp::create`/`MemDescReshapeOp::create`
   - lib/Conversion/TritonToTritonGPU/TritonToTritonGPUPass.cpp:293 update the `can_reorder=False` comment (cat lowering may need re-evaluation now that reordering is gone)

4) Python frontend/runtime:
   - python/src/ir.cc:1546 `create_reshape` drop `allowReorder`
   - python/triton/language/semantic.py:625 `reshape` drop `can_reorder`; update call sites at ~644 (`cat`), ~670 (`join`), ~1698 (`reduction` reshape to `[numel]`)
   - python/triton/language/core.py: reshape/view/cat/dot — keep `can_reorder` as an ignored backwards-compat kwarg in `reshape`/`ravel`, drop internal `_semantic.reshape(..., can_reorder=...)` calls (~1785,1890,1906,2049-2057)
   - python/triton/language/standard.py:69 `ravel` keep `can_reorder` arg but ignore it
   - python/triton/experimental/gluon/language/_semantic.py:217 `GluonSemantic.reshape` drop `can_reorder`; update reduction reshape at ~441
   - python/triton/runtime/interpreter.py:625 `create_reshape` drop `allow_reorder`

5) Tests / unit tests:
   - unittest/Dialect/TritonGPU/DialectTest.cpp:166/191/467 `inferReshapeOpEncoding` calls (drop the allow-reorder argument if still present)
   - Update the vendored .mlir tests that use `allow_reorder` (test/TritonGPU/canonicalize.mlir, test/TritonGPU/combine.mlir, test/TritonGPU/optimize-locality.mlir, test/TritonGPU/loop-pipeline-hip.mlir, test/TritonGPU/amd/*.mlir, test/Triton/combine.mlir, test/Triton/ops.mlir) to match the new assembly syntax and expected-output changes.

Note: triton-ascend's checked-out HEAD appears partially synced already (Dialect.h, Gluon/TritonGPU Dialect.cpp, and the unittest already use the 5-arg `inferReshapeOpEncoding`), but TritonOps.td, Ops.cpp, the transforms, and the Python layer still use the old `allow_reorder`/`can_reorder` API, so a full, consistent sync of this commit plus the Ascend-specific rework above is still required.
deep_analysis.risk: High. (1) `inferReshapeOpEncoding` is a pure-virtual interface; an inconsistent port (header updated but tablegen/Ops.cpp/transforms not) leaves the build broken. (2) `getAllowReorder()` was load-bearing in Ascend-specific passes — `RemoveLayoutConversions::isLayoutAnchor`, `Combine.cpp`, and especially `OptimizeThreadLocality` (the removed `OptimizeReshapeLayoutPattern`) — so these need semantic rework, not just mechanical edits, and removing them may change layout-propagation/anchor behavior and thus generated code/correctness. (3) The `cat` lowering in TritonToTritonGPUPass and Gluon `cat`/`reduction` paths currently assert on `can_reorder`; after removal their reshape-based lowering must be re-validated. (4) Broad blast radius across vendored .mlir tests (CHECK lines/expected layouts change as seen upstream, e.g. new `#ttg.linear` reshapes with explicit `ttg.convert_layout` inserted), requiring careful test regeneration to avoid silent regressions.

commits.message:
[Runtime] Serialize Gluon function constexprs for preload (#12514)

JIT cache hooks fail with `TypeError: Object of type GluonJITFunction is
not JSON serializable` when a Gluon kernel takes a `@gluon.jit` function
as a constexpr argument, even though ordinary compilation accepts it.

`serialize_specialization_data` matched function references by the exact
class name `JITFunction`, which excludes subclasses such as
`GluonJITFunction`. Gluon functions are already registered in
`_triton_jit_function_registry`, which preload uses to resolve
references, so decoding needs no change.

Signed-off-by: Prajapati, Dimple <dimple.prajapati@amd.com>
